newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen end up on BOJ economic report.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen end up on BOJ economic report.

text.p: July 24 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (H) 99.09 99.06

The key March three-month euroyen futures contract settled higher on Thursday after the Bank of Japan's quarterly economic report. Traders said the central bank appeared to have toned down its outlook for the economy.
"The report confirmed that an imminent change in monetary policy is unlikely," a city bank trader said.
"The BOJ seems to have toned down its economic outlook," said a trader for a foreign brokerage house.
The March contract's day session turnover was 55,053 lots.
The city bank trader said the BOJ's report showed the central bank expected weakness in the economy, especially with regard to capital spending.
The report said capital spending was unlikely to gather significant momentum for the time being due to an absence of rapidly expanding industries and remaining balance sheet adjustment pressures.
Earlier, a major U.S. hedge fund was detected buying about 8,000 contracts worth of the December contract, the trader with the foreign brokerage house said.
"A major hedge fund had been buying the December since this morning. They were building up new long positions," the trader said.
It was unclear, however, whether the hedge fund had been buying on speculation that the BOJ's report would contain weak forecasts, the trader said.
The key March contract's next targets would likely be 99.13 and then 99.18, a trader at a major brokerage said.
The BOJ injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market in the morning against a projected fund surplus of 100 billion yen.
The weighted average of the key overnight call rate was likely to be 0.48 percent on Thursday, unchanged from Wednesday, traders said.
The key overnight call rate was unlikely to fall significantly even if the BOJ kept providing the market with an ample fund surplus, a trader for another city bank said.
"Strong month-end fund demand, the need to roll-over maturing instruments, and demand for funds at the short end, are likely to keep the overnight call rate firm," he said.
About 65 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit had been issued at 0.67 percent as of 0703 GMT.
About 35 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.59 percent. Two-month CDs were offered at 0.59 percent.
The large issue volume of three-month CDs on Wednesday had been due to the need of borrowers to roll-over maturing CDs, a trader at another city bank said.
But the relatively healthy issue volume on Thursday was due to investor buying, the trader said. One investor bought about 50 billion yen worth of three-month CDs at 0.67 percent, he said.
-- Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-5473-3748
